141	from .model import GridMap, Position, Robot, Task
142	from .pathfinding import shortest_path
143	
144	CHECKPOINT_VERSION = 2
145	_LEGACY_VERSIONS = frozenset({1})
146	_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS = frozenset({CHECKPOINT_VERSION}) | _LEGACY_VERSIONS
147	
148	
149	def _is_int(value: object) -> bool:
150	    """JSON booleans are ints in Python; checkpoints treat them as wrong."""
151	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
152	
153	
154	def _as_cell(value: object, description: str) -> Position:
155	    """Validate a user supplied coordinate as a two-integer pair."""
156	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, (tuple, list)):
157	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
158	    if len(value) != 2:
159	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
160	    if not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value):
161	        raise ValueError(f"{description} coordinates must be integers, not booleans or other types")
162	    return value[0], value[1]
163	
164	
165	def _as_pair(value: object, description: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
166	    if (
167	        not isinstance(value, list)
168	        or len(value) != 2
169	        or not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value)
170	    ):
171	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
172	    return value[0], value[1]
173	
174	
175	def _task_route_waypoints(origin: Position, task: Task) -> list[Position]:
176	    """Required remaining visit points after *origin* for *task*.
177	
178	    The same pickup/delivery rule is used by first-time assignment, rerouting
179	    after map changes (and the recovery/sidestep planning that shares it) and
180	    checkpoint validation, so the requirement lives in exactly one place:
181	
182	    * Goods not yet collected: the route must still reach the pickup and then
183	      the dropoff. Standing exactly on the pickup makes the pickup leg empty --
184	      the leg contributes no waypoint -- but planning never collects or
185	      completes anything by itself.
186	    * Goods already collected: the robot routes straight to the dropoff, even
187	      when the old pickup cell was closed afterwards; it is never sent back.
188	
189	    When *origin*, pickup and dropoff coincide the list is empty, which
190	    describes a feasible zero-step route and must not be confused with an
191	    unreachable one.
192	    """
193	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
194	    if not task.picked_up and origin != task.pickup:
195	        waypoints.append(task.pickup)
196	    last = waypoints[-1] if waypoints else origin
197	    if task.dropoff != last:
198	        waypoints.append(task.dropoff)
199	    return waypoints
200	
201	
202	def _plan_task_route(
203	    grid: GridMap, origin: Position, task: Task
204	) -> list[Position] | None:
205	    """Shortest feasible route through the task's required waypoints.
206	
207	    The returned list holds the cells after *origin* only, concatenating the
208	    deterministic shortest legs between consecutive required points. It is
209	    ``None`` when any required point cannot be reached, and an empty list for a
210	    feasible route with zero steps (origin already at the only destination).
211	    """
212	    route: list[Position] = []
213	    current = origin
214	    for waypoint in _task_route_waypoints(origin, task):
215	        try:
216	            leg = shortest_path(grid, current, waypoint)
217	        except ValueError:
218	            return None
219	        route.extend(leg)
220	        current = waypoint
221	    return route
222	
223	
224	class FleetSimulator:
225	    def __init__(self, grid: GridMap, robots: list[Robot], tasks: list[Task]) -> None:
226	        self.grid = grid
227	        # The map as built before any runtime edit; map-change history is
228	        # replayed against this baseline.
229	        self.base_grid = grid
230	        self.robots = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
231	        self.tasks = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
232	        self.tick = 0
233	        self.replay: list[dict[str, object]] = []
234	        self.map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
235	        self._map_sequence = 0
236	        self.paused_tasks: set[str] = set()
237	        # Consecutive per-robot waits caused purely by other robots:
238	        # robot_id -> {"blocked_by": [robot_id, ...], "ticks": int}.
239	        self._traffic_waits: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
240	        positions = [robot.position for robot in robots]
241	        if len(positions) != len(set(positions)):
242	            raise ValueError("robots cannot share an initial position")
243	        if any(not grid.traversable(position) for position in positions):
244	            raise ValueError("robot starts outside traversable map space")
245	
246	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
247	    # Dynamic map edits
248	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
249	
250	    def modify_obstacles(
251	        self,
252	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
253	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
254	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
255	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
256	
257	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
258	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
259	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
260	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
261	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
262	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
263	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
264	
265	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
266	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
267	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
268	        distance is accumulated.
269	        """
270	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
271	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
272	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
273	        if conflict:
274	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
275	            raise ValueError(
276	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
277	            )
278	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
279	        for cell in add_cells:
280	            if cell in occupied:
281	                raise ValueError(
282	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
283	                )
284	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)
285	
286	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
287	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
288	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
289	        seen: set[Position] = set()
290	        ordered: list[Position] = []
291	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
292	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
293	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
294	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
295	            if position in seen:
296	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
297	                continue
298	            seen.add(position)
299	            ordered.append(position)
300	        return ordered
301	
302	    def _apply_map_change(
303	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
304	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
305	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
306	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
307	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
308	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
309	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
310	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
311	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
312	
313	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
314	        # known to change the map.
315	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
316	        self._map_sequence += 1
317	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
318	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
319	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
320	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
321	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
322	        return copy.deepcopy(record)
323	
324	    def _map_change_record(
325	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
326	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
327	        return {
328	            "type": "map_change",
329	            "tick": self.tick,
330	            "sequence": sequence,
331	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
332	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
333	        }

335	    def _plan_route(
336	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
337	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
338	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
339	
340	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
341	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
342	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
343	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
344	        """
345	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
346	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)
347	
348	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
349	        for task in self.tasks.values():
350	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
351	                continue
352	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
353	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
354	                continue
355	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
356	            if route is None:
357	                robot.route = []
358	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
359	            else:
360	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
361	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
362	                robot.route = route
363	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
364	
365	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
366	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
367	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
368	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
369	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
370	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
371	                continue
372	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
373	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
374	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
375	                continue
376	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
377	            if route is None:
378	                robot.route = []
379	                continue
380	            robot.route = route
381	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
382	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)

388	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
389	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
390	        cells: set[Position] = set()
391	        for robot in self.robots.values():
392	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
393	                cells.update(robot.route)
394	        return cells
395	
396	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
397	        self,
398	        blocker: Robot,
399	        requester: Robot,
400	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
401	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
402	    ) -> Position | None:
403	        """Free side-cell an idle blocker can yield to, or None.
404	
405	        The target may not be the requester's own cell (that would swap the
406	        two robots within one tick) nor any cell another robot still plans to
407	        drive through, so the blocker never trades one blockage for another.
408	        """
409	        on_routes = self._route_cells(exclude_id=blocker.robot_id)
410	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(blocker.position):
411	            if cell == requester.position:
412	                continue
413	            if cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
414	                continue
415	            if cell in on_routes:
416	                continue
417	            return cell
418	        return None
419	
420	    def _self_sidestep(
421	        self,
422	        robot: Robot,
423	        task: Task | None,
424	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
425	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
426	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
427	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
428	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
429	
430	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
431	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
432	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
433	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
434	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
435	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
436	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
437	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
438	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
439	        """
440	        if task is None or task.completed:
441	            return None
442	        destination = robot.route[0]
443	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
444	        if blocker_id is None:
445	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
446	        on_routes = self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id)
447	        best: tuple[int, int, Position, list[Position]] | None = None
448	        for index, cell in enumerate(self.grid.neighbors(robot.position)):
449	            if cell in occupied or cell in reserved or cell in on_routes:
450	                continue
451	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
452	            if route is None:
453	                continue
454	            if (
455	                blocker_id is not None
456	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
457	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
458	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
459	                )
460	            ):
461	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
462	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
463	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
464	                continue
465	            if best is None or (len(route), index) < (best[0], best[1]):
466	                best = (len(route), index, cell, route)
467	        if best is None:
468	            return None
469	        return best[2], best[3]
470	
471	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
472	        self,
473	        robot: Robot,
474	        side: Position,
475	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
476	        blocker_id: str,
477	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
478	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
479	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
480	    ) -> bool:
481	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
482	
483	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
484	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
485	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
486	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
487	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
488	        never rejected here.
489	        """
490	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
491	            return False
492	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
493	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
494	            return False
495	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
496	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
497	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
498	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
499	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id
500	        # The requester only gets back onto its route by driving through these
501	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
502	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
503	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
504	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
505	        return not self._can_vacate(
506	            blocker,
507	            robot,
508	            hyp_occupied,
509	            reserved,
510	            frozenset({robot.robot_id}) | already_moved,
511	            blocked_path,
512	        )
513	
514	    def _can_vacate(
515	        self,
516	        blocker: Robot,
517	        requester: Robot,
518	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
519	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
520	        checking: frozenset[str],
521	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
522	    ) -> bool:
523	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
524	
525	        An idle blocker leaves only by yielding onto a safe side cell for the
526	        requesting robot; a busy blocker leaves by driving onto its next
527	        waypoint (possibly following a chain of robots that all move this tick)
528	        or by sidestepping onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by
529	        map unreachability never move. *checking* names robots whose leave
530	        check is already on the call stack, so a cyclic dependency (a head-on
531	        deadlock, or the requester itself) is not assumed resolvable.
532	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive back
533	        through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so such
534	        sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on the
535	        blocker's own route does).
536	        """
537	        if blocker.robot_id in checking:
538	            return False
539	        task = self.tasks[blocker.task_id] if blocker.task_id is not None else None
540	        if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
541	            return False
542	        if task is not None and not blocker.route:
543	            # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this tick;
544	            # it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
545	            return False
546	        if task is None:
547	            # Idle robots only ever move by yielding for a requester.
548	            side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, requester, occupied, reserved)
549	            return side is not None and side not in blocked_path
550	        if blocker.route:
551	            ahead = blocker.route[0]
552	            if (
553	                self.grid.traversable(ahead)
554	                and ahead not in occupied
555	                and ahead not in reserved
556	            ):
557	                return True
558	            occupant_id = occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
559	            if (
560	                occupant_id is not None
561	                and occupant_id != blocker.robot_id
562	                and occupant_id not in checking
563	            ):
564	                # The blocker could follow the robot ahead once that robot
565	                # vacates its cell this same tick.
566	                if self._can_vacate(
567	                    self.robots[occupant_id],
568	                    requester,
569	                    occupied,
570	                    reserved,
571	                    checking | {blocker.robot_id},
572	                    blocked_path,
573	                ):
574	                    return True
575	        # Otherwise the blocker might sidestep onto a free side cell itself,
576	        # but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has to use.
577	        on_routes = self._route_cells(exclude_id=blocker.robot_id)
578	        for side_cell in self.grid.neighbors(blocker.position):
579	            if (
580	                side_cell in occupied
581	                or side_cell in reserved
582	                or side_cell in on_routes
583	                or side_cell in blocked_path
584	            ):
585	                continue
586	            if self._plan_route(blocker, task, start=side_cell) is not None:
587	                return True
588	        return False
589	
590	    def _update_traffic_waits(
591	        self,
592	        waited: dict[str, str],
593	        moved_ids: frozenset[str],
594	    ) -> None:
595	        """Keep only waits that still hold once the tick's moves have settled.
596	
597	        *waited* maps every robot that stopped this tick purely because
598	        another robot held its next waypoint to the robot it saw there at the
599	        time; *moved_ids* names the robots that ended up moving. The mid-tick
600	        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
601	        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
602	        A record survives only when the robot neither moved nor paused and its
603	        next waypoint is occupied by another robot in the final layout; the
604	        reported blocker is whichever robot actually occupies that cell. Any
605	        other outcome -- the robot moved, its task paused, or the way ahead
606	        cleared -- deletes the entry. A wait that continues without a free tick
607	        in between keeps accumulating even when the blocker changes identity;
608	        once interrupted, a later blockage starts a fresh count at one.
609	        """
610	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
611	        surviving: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
612	        for robot_id in waited:
613	            if robot_id in moved_ids:
614	                continue
615	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
616	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
617	                continue
618	            task = self.tasks.get(robot.task_id) if robot.task_id is not None else None
619	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
620	                continue
621	            blocker_id = occupied.get(robot.route[0])
622	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot_id:
623	                continue
624	            entry = self._traffic_waits.get(robot_id)
625	            if entry is None:
626	                surviving[robot_id] = {"blocked_by": [blocker_id], "ticks": 1}
627	            else:
628	                surviving[robot_id] = {
629	                    "blocked_by": [blocker_id],
630	                    "ticks": int(entry["ticks"]) + 1,
631	                }
632	        self._traffic_waits = surviving
633	
634	    def _reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change(self) -> None:
635	        """Drop wait records an accepted map edit has invalidated.
636	
637	        A map change never moves a robot, so it can neither create a wait nor
638	        add to one; but it can end one. A robot whose task just paused on
639	        unreachability has no route left to wait on, and a robot whose
640	        replanned next cell is no longer held by the recorded blocker is not
641	        blocked by it anymore -- both records are removed. An entry whose
642	        robot still faces the very same blocker on its refreshed route keeps
643	        its count untouched, whatever else the edit changed.
644	        """
645	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
646	        for robot_id, entry in list(self._traffic_waits.items()):
647	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
648	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
649	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
650	                continue
651	            if occupied.get(robot.route[0]) not in entry["blocked_by"]:
652	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
653	
654	    def _traffic_wait_report(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
655	        return [
656	            {
657	                "robot_id": robot_id,
658	                "blocked_by": list(entry["blocked_by"]),
659	                "ticks": entry["ticks"],
660	            }
661	            for robot_id, entry in sorted(self._traffic_waits.items())
662	        ]

668	    def assign_tasks(self) -> None:
669	        """Assign pending tasks to the nearest idle robot using stable tie breaks."""
670	        pending = [task for task in self.tasks.values() if task.assigned_robot is None]
671	        for task in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: item.task_id):
672	            choices: list[tuple[int, str, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = []
673	            for robot in self.robots.values():
674	                if not robot.idle:
675	                    continue
676	                route = _plan_task_route(self.grid, robot.position, task)
677	                if route is None:
678	                    continue
679	                choices.append((len(route), robot.robot_id, route))
680	            if not choices:
681	                # No robot can reach this task yet; it keeps waiting and does
682	                # not block assignment of other tasks.
683	                continue
684	            _, robot_id, route = min(choices)
685	            robot = self.robots[robot_id]
686	            robot.task_id = task.task_id
687	            robot.route = route
688	            task.assigned_robot = robot_id
689	
690	    def _confirm_pickups(self) -> None:
691	        """A robot starting a tick on its pickup point collects first."""
692	        for robot in self.robots.values():
693	            if robot.task_id is None:
694	                continue
695	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
696	            if not task.completed and not task.picked_up and robot.position == task.pickup:
697	                task.picked_up = True
698	
699	    def step(self) -> dict[str, object]:
700	        self._confirm_pickups()
701	        self._recover_paused_tasks()
702	        self.assign_tasks()
703	        # A robot assigned while already standing on the pickup cell collects
704	        # immediately instead of driving off without the goods.
705	        self._confirm_pickups()
706	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
707	        reserved: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {}
708	        moved: list[str] = []
709	        moved_ids: set[str] = set()
710	        blocked_by: dict[str, str] = {}
711	
712	        def relocate(robot: Robot, destination: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
713	            del occupied[robot.position]
714	            robot.position = destination
715	            robot.distance_travelled += 1
716	            occupied[destination] = robot.robot_id
717	            reserved[destination] = robot.robot_id
718	            moved.append(robot.robot_id)
719	            moved_ids.add(robot.robot_id)
720	
721	        for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id):
722	            if robot.robot_id in moved_ids:
723	                # Already yielded this tick at another robot's request.
724	                continue
725	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id] if robot.task_id is not None else None
726	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
727	                # Paused by map unreachability: stays put, never yields.
728	                continue
729	            if not robot.route:
730	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
731	                continue
732	            destination = robot.route[0]
733	            if not self.grid.traversable(destination):
734	                # Defensive: routes are normally replanned on every map edit.
735	                if task is not None and not task.completed:
736	                    route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
737	                    if route is None:
738	                        robot.route = []
739	                        self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
740	                    else:
741	                        robot.route = route
742	                continue
743	            blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
744	            if blocker_id is None:
745	                blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
746	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot.robot_id:
747	                relocate(robot, destination)
748	                robot.route.pop(0)
749	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
750	                continue
751	            # Another robot is in the way; this is distinct from a
752	            # map-unreachability pause and the task stays active.
753	            blocker = self.robots[blocker_id]
754	            if blocker_id not in moved_ids:
755	                if blocker.task_id is None:
756	                    # Idle blocker: ask it to yield onto a free side cell,
757	                    # then take over the cell it vacated.
758	                    side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, robot, occupied, reserved)
759	                    if side is not None:
760	                        relocate(blocker, side)
761	                        relocate(robot, destination)
762	                        robot.route.pop(0)
763	                        self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
764	                        continue
765	                elif blocker.route:
766	                    ahead = blocker.route[0]
767	                    if (
768	                        self.grid.traversable(ahead)
769	                        and ahead not in occupied
770	                        and ahead not in reserved
771	                    ):
772	                        # The blocker is expected to drive on within this
773	                        # tick, so waiting one tick is cheaper than detouring.
774	                        blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
775	                        continue
776	            # The blocker cannot or will not move this tick: try to sidestep
777	            # onto a free adjacent cell and replan from there.
778	            side = self._self_sidestep(
779	                robot, task, occupied, reserved, frozenset(moved_ids)
780	            )
781	            if side is not None:
782	                cell, route = side
783	                relocate(robot, cell)
784	                robot.route = route
785	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
786	                continue
787	            blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
788	        self._update_traffic_waits(blocked_by, frozenset(moved_ids))
789	        self.tick += 1
790	        event: dict[str, object] = {
791	            "type": "tick",
792	            "tick": self.tick,
793	            "moved": moved,
794	            "robots": {robot_id: list(robot.position) for robot_id, robot in sorted(self.robots.items())},
795	            "completed": sorted(task.task_id for task in self.tasks.values() if task.completed),
796	        }
797	        self.replay.append(event)
798	        return event
799	
800	    def _finish_if_arrived(self, robot: Robot) -> None:
801	        if robot.task_id is None:
802	            return
803	        task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
804	        if task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
805	            return
806	        if robot.position == task.pickup:
807	            task.picked_up = True
808	        if task.picked_up and robot.position == task.dropoff and not robot.route:
809	            task.completed = True
810	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
811	            robot.task_id = None
812

816	            "ticks": self.tick,

818	            "tasks_completed": completed,
819	            "tasks_paused": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
820	            "completion_ratio": completed / len(self.tasks) if self.tasks else 1.0,
821	            "distance_total": sum(robot.distance_travelled for robot in self.robots.values()),
822	            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
823	        }

853	    def save_checkpoint(self, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> None:
854	        """Write the simulator state to *path* without changing this instance.
855	
856	        The write is atomic: an existing destination keeps either its complete
857	        old contents or the complete new contents, and a brand-new destination
858	        is either fully created or left absent. Filesystem or permission errors
859	        raise :class:`OSError`.
860	        """
861	        document = {
862	            "version": CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
863	            "grid": {
864	                "width": self.grid.width,
865	                "height": self.grid.height,
866	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.grid.obstacles)],
867	            },
868	            "base_grid": {
869	                "width": self.base_grid.width,
870	                "height": self.base_grid.height,
871	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.base_grid.obstacles)],
872	            },
873	            "tick": self.tick,
874	            "robots": [
875	                {
876	                    "robot_id": robot.robot_id,
877	                    "position": list(robot.position),
878	                    "route": [list(cell) for cell in robot.route],
879	                    "task_id": robot.task_id,
880	                    "distance_travelled": robot.distance_travelled,
881	                }
882	                for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id)
883	            ],
884	            "tasks": [
885	                {
886	                    "task_id": task.task_id,

955	    @classmethod
956	    def _from_checkpoint(cls, data: object) -> FleetSimulator:
957	        if not isinstance(data, dict):

960	        version = data.get("version")
961	        if not _is_int(version):
962	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'version' must be an integer")
963	        if version not in _SUPPORTED_VERSIONS:
964	            raise ValueError(
965	                f"unsupported checkpoint version {version}; supported versions: "
966	                f"{sorted(_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS)}"
967	            )
968	
969	        grid = cls._load_grid(data)
970	        tick = cls._load_tick(data)
971	        robot_records, task_records = cls._load_entities(data)
972	
973	        map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
974	        paused: set[str] = set()
975	        if version == 1:
976	            replay = cls._load_legacy_replay(data)

978	        else:
979	            replay = cls._load_replay(data)
980	            map_changes = cls._load_map_changes(data)
981	            paused = cls._load_paused_tasks(data)
982	            base_grid = cls._load_base_grid(data)
983	            if (base_grid.width, base_grid.height) != (grid.width, grid.height):
984	                raise ValueError("base grid dimensions must match the current grid")

986	
987	        robots: list[Robot] = []
988	        for record in robot_records:
989	            position = _as_pair(record["position"], f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position")
990	            if not grid.traversable(position):
991	                raise ValueError(
992	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position {list(position)} is outside "
993	                    "the map or inside an obstacle"
994	                )
995	            route: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
996	            previous = position
997	            for index, cell in enumerate(record["route"]):
998	                waypoint = _as_pair(
999	                    cell, f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {index}"
1000	                )
1001	                if not grid.traversable(waypoint):
1002	                    raise ValueError(
1003	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {list(waypoint)} is "
1004	                        "outside the map or inside an obstacle"
1005	                    )
1006	                if abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0]) + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1]) != 1:
1007	                    raise ValueError(
1008	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
1009	                        f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
1010	                    )
1011	                route.append(waypoint)
1012	                previous = waypoint
1013	            distance = record["distance_travelled"]
1014	            if not _is_int(distance) or distance < 0:
1015	                raise ValueError(
1016	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} distance_travelled must be a "
1017	                    "non-negative integer"
1018	                )
1019	            robots.append(Robot(record["robot_id"], position, route, record["task_id"], distance))
1020	
1021	        tasks: list[Task] = []
1022	        for record in task_records:
1023	            pickup = _as_pair(record["pickup"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} pickup")
1024	            dropoff = _as_pair(record["dropoff"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} dropoff")
1025	            tasks.append(
1026	                Task(
1027	                    record["task_id"],
1028	                    pickup,
1029	                    dropoff,
1030	                    record["assigned_robot"],
1031	                    record["picked_up"],
1032	                    record["completed"],
1033	                )
1034	            )
1035	
1036	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
1037	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
1038	
1039	        for robot in robots:
1040	            if robot.task_id is not None:
1041	                task = task_by_id.get(robot.task_id)
1042	                if task is None:
1043	                    raise ValueError(
1044	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes unknown task {robot.task_id!r}"
1045	                    )
1046	                if task.completed:
1047	                    raise ValueError(
1048	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} that is "
1049	                        "already completed"
1050	                    )
1051	                if task.assigned_robot != robot.robot_id:
1052	                    raise ValueError(
1053	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} but the "
1054	                        f"task is assigned to {task.assigned_robot!r}"
1055	                    )
1056	        for task in tasks:
1057	            if task.completed and not task.picked_up:
1058	                raise ValueError(f"task {task.task_id!r} is completed but never picked up")
1059	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
1060	                raise ValueError(
1061	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
1062	                )
1063	            # Completed tasks retain historical ownership; their robots are free
1064	            # to take new work, so the mutual binding only holds while a task is
1065	            # still in progress.
1066	            if not task.completed and task.assigned_robot is not None:
1067	                owner = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
1068	                if owner is None:
1069	                    raise ValueError(
1070	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is assigned to unknown robot "
1071	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r}"
1072	                    )
1073	                if owner.task_id != task.task_id:
1074	                    raise ValueError(
1075	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} claims robot {owner.robot_id!r} but the "
1076	                        f"robot executes {owner.task_id!r}"
1077	                    )
1078	
1079	        cls._validate_paused_state(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id, grid)
1080	        cls._validate_active_task_routes(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id)
1081	        traffic_waits = cls._load_traffic_waits(data, robot_by_id)
1082	
1083	        replay_change_frames = cls._replay_map_change_frames(replay)
1084	        if replay_change_frames != map_changes:
1085	            raise ValueError("replay map-change frames do not match 'map_changes' history")
1086	
1087	        simulator = cls(grid, robots, tasks)
1088	        simulator.base_grid = base_grid
1089	        simulator.tick = tick
1090	        simulator.replay = copy.deepcopy(replay)
1091	        simulator.map_changes = copy.deepcopy(map_changes)
1092	        simulator._map_sequence = len(map_changes)
1093	        simulator.paused_tasks = set(paused)
1094	        simulator._traffic_waits = traffic_waits

1096	        # applies to every tick frame. Version 2 replays the recorded changes
1097	        # alongside the frames so each frame is judged against its contemporary
1098	        # map.
1099	        cls._validate_replay_positions(replay, tick, robot_by_id, base_grid, map_changes)

1168	        cls, data: Mapping[str, object]

1170	        raw_robots = cls._require_field(data, "robots")

1172	        if not isinstance(raw_robots, list):

1174	        if not isinstance(raw_tasks, list):
1175	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'tasks' must be a list")
1176	
1177	        robot_records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1178	        robot_ids: set[str] = set()

1180	            if not isinstance(record, dict):
1181	                raise ValueError(f"robot entry {index} must be an object")
1182	            robot_id = record.get("robot_id")
1183	            if not isinstance(robot_id, str):
1184	                raise ValueError(f"robot entry {index} field 'robot_id' must be a string")
1185	            if robot_id in robot_ids:
1186	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate robot id {robot_id!r} in checkpoint")
1187	            robot_ids.add(robot_id)

1189	            if task_id is not None and not isinstance(task_id, str):
1190	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} field 'task_id' must be a string or null")
1191	            if "position" not in record:
1192	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} is missing field 'position'")
1193	            route = record.get("route")
1194	            if not isinstance(route, list):
1195	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} field 'route' must be a list")
1196	            if "distance_travelled" not in record:
1197	                raise ValueError(f"robot {robot_id!r} is missing field 'distance_travelled'")

1201	        task_ids: set[str] = set()
1202	        for index, record in enumerate(raw_tasks):
1203	            if not isinstance(record, dict):
1204	                raise ValueError(f"task entry {index} must be an object")
1205	            task_id = record.get("task_id")
1206	            if not isinstance(task_id, str):
1207	                raise ValueError(f"task entry {index} field 'task_id' must be a string")
1208	            if task_id in task_ids:

1210	            task_ids.add(task_id)

1212	            if assigned is not None and not isinstance(assigned, str):
1213	                raise ValueError(
1214	                    f"task {task_id!r} field 'assigned_robot' must be a string or null"
1215	                )

1217	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} field 'picked_up' must be a boolean")
1218	            if not isinstance(record.get("completed"), bool):
1219	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} field 'completed' must be a boolean")
1220	            if "pickup" not in record:
1221	                raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} is missing field 'pickup'")
1222	            if "dropoff" not in record:

1249	    @classmethod
1250	    def _load_map_changes(cls, data: Mapping[str, object]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
1251	        raw = cls._require_field(data, "map_changes")
1252	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
1253	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'map_changes' must be a list")
1254	        changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1255	        last_tick = -1
1256	        last_sequence = 0
1257	        for index, frame in enumerate(raw):
1258	            context = f"map change {index}"
1259	            if not isinstance(frame, dict):
1260	                raise ValueError(f"{context} must be an object")
1261	            tick = frame.get("tick")
1262	            sequence = frame.get("sequence")
1263	            if not _is_int(tick) or tick < 0:
1264	                raise ValueError(f"{context} field 'tick' must be a non-negative integer")
1265	            if not _is_int(sequence) or sequence <= 0:
1266	                raise ValueError(f"{context} field 'sequence' must be a positive integer")
1267	            if sequence != index + 1:
1268	                raise ValueError(
1269	                    f"map change sequences must run consecutively from 1; change {index} "
1270	                    f"has sequence {sequence}, expected {index + 1}"
1271	                )
1272	            if tick < last_tick:
1273	                raise ValueError(
1274	                    f"{context} tick {tick} is earlier than a preceding map change"
1275	                )
1276	            if tick == last_tick and sequence != last_sequence + 1:
1277	                raise ValueError(f"{context} breaks consecutive sequencing at tick {tick}")
1278	            added = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("added"), context, "added")
1279	            removed = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("removed"), context, "removed")
1280	            if not added and not removed:
1281	                raise ValueError(f"{context} contains no actual obstacle changes")
1282	            overlap = set(added) & set(removed)
1283	            if overlap:
1284	                cell = sorted(overlap)[0]
1285	                raise ValueError(
1286	                    f"{context} adds and removes the same cell {list(cell)}"
1287	                )
1288	            changes.append(
1289	                {
1290	                    "type": "map_change",
1291	                    "tick": tick,
1292	                    "sequence": sequence,
1293	                    "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
1294	                    "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
1295	                }
1296	            )
1297	            last_tick = tick
1298	            last_sequence = sequence
1299	        return changes

1301	    @classmethod
1302	    def _validate_map_history(
1303	        cls,
1304	        base_grid: GridMap,
1305	        saved_grid: GridMap,
1306	        changes: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
1307	    ) -> None:
1308	        obstacles = set(base_grid.obstacles)
1309	        width, height = saved_grid.width, saved_grid.height
1310	        for frame in changes:
1311	            for key in ("added", "removed"):
1312	                for cell in frame[key]:
1313	                    x, y = cell
1314	                    if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height):
1315	                        raise ValueError(
1316	                            f"map change {frame['sequence']} cell {list(cell)} lies "
1317	                            "outside the map"
1318	                        )
1319	            added = {tuple(cell) for cell in frame["added"]}
1320	            removed = {tuple(cell) for cell in frame["removed"]}
1321	            for cell in added:
1322	                if cell in obstacles:
1323	                    raise ValueError(
1324	                        f"map change {frame['sequence']} adds obstacle {list(cell)} "
1325	                        "that is already present according to the history"
1326	                    )
1327	            for cell in removed:
1328	                if cell not in obstacles:
1329	                    raise ValueError(
1330	                        f"map change {frame['sequence']} removes obstacle {list(cell)} "
1331	                        "that is absent according to the history"
1332	                    )
1333	            obstacles |= added
1334	            obstacles -= removed
1335	        if obstacles != set(saved_grid.obstacles):
1336	            raise ValueError(
1337	                "the map reproduced from 'map_changes' does not match the saved grid"
1338	            )

1367	    def _load_traffic_waits(
1368	        cls, data: Mapping[str, object], robot_by_id: Mapping[str, Robot]

1376	        for index, entry in enumerate(raw):
